text:
claire: New hire hit a weird onboarding blocker during cred rotation in the dockerized sampleapp. They replaced the API key in container env via CI but app kept failing with 401.
devon: What's the exact setup?
claire: The sampleapp runs in a docker container started from our onboarding image. The image has a .env baked at build time (we did that for convenience). CI rotates creds by injecting env vars on `docker run` but the app re-reads the .env file on startup and prioritizes it over process env.
rafa: Oof, so the container ends up using stale creds from .env even though CI injected new ones. That explains the "suddenly broken after rotation" report.
sam: Any error visible?
claire: App log shows: `401 Unauthorized: invalid key scope` when calling /v1/generate. No extra diagnostic headers.
devon: Could be compounded by env var name mismatch. Which env var are we using for project scoping?
claire: Sampleapp README references REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_ORG only. The docker image .env had REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME set to "onboard-demo". Our Go SDK reads REDWOOD_PROJECT, Node SDK reads REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME. CI injects REDWOOD_PROJECT. So sometimes you get two different names set in different places.
rafa: So three failure modes: 1) creds baked in .env override runtime, 2) env var name mismatch across SDKs, 3) SDK retry behavior treats 401 as transient and spins.
sam: Proposed quick wins: - sampleapp: stop baking .env into image; prefer runtime env. Add explicit startup check: if REDWOOD_API_KEY set and no detected project env -> exit 1 with clear msg. - SDKs: accept both REDWOOD_PROJECT and REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME, prefer REDWOOD_PROJECT. Log which var was used. - Retry policy: treat 401/403 as non-retry unless response has Retry-After or header `x-redwood-retryable-auth: true`.
devon: Also add a small integration test for containers: run the onboarding image with a different REDWOOD_API_KEY passed via `docker run -e` and assert the app uses it (e.g., hits /health which calls list-models).
rafa: For diagnostics, backend could add `x-redwood-expected-scope: project` header when rejecting due to missing project scope, and `x-redwood-provided-scope: none|project=xxx` to help debug.
claire: I'll patch the sampleapp to read env precedence: process env -> .env file only if explicitly allowed by STARTUP_USE_DOTENV=true. Also add a startup smoke check that fails with: `AuthError: missing project scope. Set REDWOOD_PROJECT or export REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME for older tools.`
sam: I'll open parity PRs for Node/Java/Go with the env fallback and unit tests. Adding a small log line: `Using project from REDWOOD_PROJECT` or `Using project from REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME`.
devon: Good. Ops: please add an onboarding CI job that runs the container with only REDWOOD_API_KEY set (no project var) to catch this early.
ops: CI job added: onboarding-container-smoke #101 queued
ci-bot: CI: onboarding-container-smoke #101 started
rafa: Also let's update onboarding docs and the quick troubleshooting snippet: - If you see 401 + `x-redwood-expected-scope: project`, ensure REDWOOD_PROJECT is set and not overridden by a baked .env.
claire: Timeline: sampleapp fix + docs today, SDK parity PRs in next 6 hours, CI smoke job to gate onboarding flows.
sam: Will include CHANGES entries and a small migration note for teams that rely on REDWOOD_PROJECT_NAME.
claire: Thanks all. Follow-ups: sam PRs, ops CI run, and backend ticket for diagnostic headers.
